title: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591: three ciphertexts to the Bavarian court, 1531-1537 (DECODE R9403, R9414, R9415; catalogue 162)

documents.shelfmark: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.226-228 (DECODE R9403)

plaintext.source: Gloss over the first lines; rest read here with the System B key rebuilt in kaa4591/sysB.

transcription.notes: Reading-aligned: sign codes written from the reading with the key (build.py), homophone variants not kept, so the count is a reconstruction.

documents.shelfmark: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.260-261 (DECODE R9415)

plaintext.source: Gloss over P1 l.3 ('incrementum') and clear passages; key rebuilt here.

transcription.notes: One char per sign; clear passages and glosses excluded by signstream.py.

documents.shelfmark: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.257-259 (DECODE R9414)

plaintext.source: Gloss over P1 l.6-8; clear opening, date and address; key rebuilt here.

transcription.notes: transcription_v2.txt, one char per sign, '?' blots counted as signs.

system.summary: Three graphic-sign ciphers: Łaski's System B (monoalphabetic with word signs, e/r swapped) for R9403, and two homophonic sign alphabets, L (R9415, Latin) and G (R9414, German), with a few word signs.
system.sibling_key: kaa4591/sysB/key_from_glosses.tsv (Łaski, from R9322/R9417) read R9403 with e/r swapped; R9369 (Augurelio 1531) and the System A′ key tested on L and G, no match
system.notes: Measured distinct signs: R9403 22 (reconstructed), R9415 51, R9414 42.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear glosses over a few lines of each letter; no edition found (web search 22 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie; the target was assigned by the user. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: DECODE images of R9403, R9414, R9415 and neighbours R9404-R9407, R9418-R9422 fetched with the cookie
R9403 read with Łaski's System B key from kaa4591/sysB
R9403: e and r swapped (⋇ = e, X = r), variant sign shapes; DAG word sign = King John
R9403 read line by line, 414/416 words
R9415 transcribed one char per sign; P1 photographed upside down
System A′ key (R9427 gloss) applied to R9415, whose signs look like A′
R9369 (Augurelio's 1531 key) tested on R9415 (L) and R9414 (G)
R9415 P1 l.3 gloss 'incrementum' seeded the key
R9415 annealing with the la model, then beam search (solve.py, beam.py)
R9415 zoom pass: join nulls after clear passages, h ligatures; 386/405 words
R9414 transcribed (v1, then v2 on line-third crops)
R9414 P1 l.6-8 gloss gave the first values of system G
R9414 annealing and de-1500s beam (beam2.py) - about 50% read
R9414 three visual passes over every line (cp12 logs): 77.1% then 91.3%
gapfill.py one-edit lexicon search over unread R9414 words
Web search for Łaski 1531, Zápolya letters to the Bavarian dukes, Augurelio, Acta Tomiciana

outcome.fraction_read_source: words of the ciphered runs: r9403/decoded.txt 414/416, r9415/count.txt 386/405, r9414 count_v2.py reading_v3.txt 947/1037; [..]/? counted unread
outcome.notes: R9403 and R9415 pass the read bar; R9414 is at 91.3%. Keys rebuilt for all three (G has ambiguous homophones).

gaps.item: R9414 code signs Ψ, swash X, K (~10 words)
R9414 blotted or struck signs (~15 words)
R9403 P3 l.11-12 two words and P1 l.4 insertion
